Maya: Quick summary from today's run — we built a p50/p95/p99 matrix across kernels + batching configs using a synthetic swingbench generator + 10k-request replay slice. Headline: quantized model + speculative decoding enabled shows a p99 regression (~+18% latency) vs baseline fp16 path, but p50 is slightly better. I captured logs and a small matrix below.

Maya: matrix (ms) `kernel | batching | kv_warm_frac | p50 | p95 | p99`
```
cuda-matmul-v1 | dynamic | 0.92 | 34 | 68 | 142
matmul-accel   | dynamic | 0.92 | 30 | 63 | 169  <-- quant+spec enabled
cuda-matmul-v1 | static  | 0.55 | 40 | 95 | 210  <-- kv cold-heavy
matmul-accel   | static  | 0.55 | 36 | 88 | 198
```

Maya: notes: speculative decoding threshold 0.85, quant profile q4_0, replay harness used 1.2x user think-time multiplier to stress tails. Full logs uploaded to /tmp/swingbench-179880.

Aj: Can you paste the exact harness invocation? I want to re-run locally and try with per-model kernel pinned.

Maya: sure — command we used:
```
./run_swingbench --replay /data/replays/10k_slice.json --mix "chat:0.7,embed:0.3" --think 1.2 --seed 42 \
  --model rwd/open-q4_0 --kernel auto --speculative 0.85 --concurrency 120
```

Sam: quick profiler snippet — large tail spikes line up with KV cache cold misses (KV miss ratio jumps from 8% -> 43% around t=00:21). stacktrace shows repeated tokenizer + KVCopy on hot path.
```
[00:20:58] tail_spike start
kv_cache.hit_rate: 0.57 -> 0.14
kernel_switch: cuda-matmul-v1 -> matmul-accel
cpu stuck on tokenizer loop (5x)
[00:21:06] speculative fallback triggered for request 3472
```

Sam: hypothesis: quant path changes memory layout causing less effective KV reuse for our current cache sharding, so more cold misses -> longer kernel warmups -> tail amplification with spec on.

Dmitri: that tracks. Two experiments to isolate:
1) disable speculative decoding and re-run the same replay (quick smoke)
2) pin kernel to cuda-matmul-v1 and measure p99 delta
Also we should run a regression-gate smoke that toggles quant profile remotely (A/B) at 1% traffic before ramp.

Maya: ran experiment 1 & 2 — results attached:
```
speculative OFF + matmul-accel -> p99: 138 (was 169)
speculative ON  + cuda-matmul-v1 -> p99: 150
cost: token/sec drops ~6% when speculative OFF
```

Maya: interpretation: speculative helps p50 but amplifies tail when KV cold fraction climbs. Turning it off reduces worst-case latency at modest throughput cost.

Aj: can we tune batching heuristics? maybe reduce max_batch_time for quantized kernels or split batching strategies by kernel type.

Dmitri: yes — propose adaptive batching rule: if kv_warm_frac < 0.7 then favor smaller max_batch_time and aggressive prefix caching. Also a hotspot: kernel selector should prefer kernels that preserve contiguous KV memory layout for quant models.

Lucy: I can run a micro-benchmark that cycles through 100k short-chat requests to profile kernel warmups and KV locality effects. Will do kernel-only sweeps (no speculative) and produce a small p99 heatmap.

Maya: thanks. Next steps agreed:
- Lucy: run microbench and upload heatmap (ETA EOD)
- Sam: instrument KV cache to emit per-shard cold_fraction metric (ETA tomorrow)
- Aj: prototype batching rule and config flags for kernel-specific batch_time (ETA 2 days)
- Dmitri: add a regression-gate test that flips quant profile at 1% traffic and watches p99 (ETA 3 days)

infra-bot: canary-deploy succeeded: infra/canary/17988 -> OK :white_check_mark:

Maya: Also: flagging alert PR-4321 for follow-up, it's the regression gate alert that fired during the run. Will file a short postmortem if this repeats. 

Maya: favorite: :eyes: if you want to review the raw logs: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/swingbench/179880 (read-only)

Aj: appreciated. I'll re-run locally with pinned kernel and report back with a diff of the perf counters.

Sam: I'll try a run with speculative but lowered threshold (0.7) to see if that reduces false fallbacks.

Dmitri: if lowered threshold helps, we can ship rule to dynamically lower speculative thresholds when kv_cold_fraction > 0.3 and fail open on regression gate.

Maya: great — we'll reconvene after those runs. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
